title: Engineering quantum criticality and dynamics on an analog-digital simulator
abstract: We explore emergent phenomena in out-of-equilibrium interacting many-body systems using neutral atom arrays with analog-digital simulation techniques. By combining analog and digital quantum operations and coherent mapping between Rydberg and hyperfine qubits, we engineer complex quantum dynamics including ring-exchange and particle hopping behaviors. We target a Rokhsar-Kivelson type quantum spin liquid state on a 271-site kagome lattice, observing many-body coherences between nearly equal-amplitude dimer configurations over up to 18 sites.
key_claims: 271-site kagome lattice quantum spin liquid with many-body coherences over 18 sites
Analog-digital hybrid technique using Rydberg + hyperfine coherent mapping
Rahul Sahay (hologron paper co-author) is an author -- same Lukin group
Demonstrates advanced control over Rydberg arrays at scales relevant to holographic simulation
Largest Rydberg simulator result in 2026 window
hardware_used: Neutral-atom Rydberg array (Harvard Lukin group), 271 atoms
